translations.seg-0001: Hey Xueling, what have you been up to lately? I haven't seen you post on WeChat Moments in ages.
translations.seg-0002: I started a Substack! It's all about Chinese translations of Mandarin-language and Taiwanese music.
translations.seg-0003: Whoa, that's pretty cool. What made you suddenly want to do that?
translations.seg-0004: I just wanted to make something original and meaningful after work. I'm the lifelong-learner type — I love picking up new things, and I want to write and research seriously.
translations.seg-0005: Got it. So what do you usually write about?
translations.seg-0006: Mostly translations of Mandarin-language and Taiwanese music, plus some of my own reflections. I talk about Chinese and Japanese philosophy, spirituality, aesthetics, that kind of thing.
translations.seg-0007: Sounds very artsy. Didn't you study fiction writing before?
translations.seg-0008: Yeah, I'm more used to being a creative writer — I'm still figuring out essays and journalism. But I'm working on it!
translations.seg-0009: So does your blog have a focus? Like, what niche are you going for?
translations.seg-0010: Honestly, I don't really want to force a niche. I'm just letting it happen naturally, around the theme of East Asian studies. We'll see how it goes!
translations.seg-0011: Haha, maximum chill. So what do you like in your free time?
translations.seg-0012: Mountains, tea, solitude. I feel a deep connection with Taoist hermits, monks and ancient poets.
translations.seg-0013: Amazing, that sounds so you. I'm subscribing for sure!
